title: Knowledge intake plan
description: The classification of received domain material into the ontology, produced by the domain-analyst agent and consumed by whatever authors the objects. The named producer is domain-analyst; the named consumer is the intake procedure, which reads `state` to decide whether to author and reads each entry to delegate one authoring call. This artifact carries control flow and is validated at the boundary before consumption, so it is a versioned schema rather than prose. It is a plan and not an authority: an entry states the node type and the `ddd` value decided for a construct, and the pairing of the two is checked by knowledge-object.json when the object is authored — duplicating the per-type vocabulary here would give one fact two homes. Gaps are expected content: material arriving from analysis does not carry the retrieval question, the declared out-of-scope, the type parameters, or the identity strategy, and nothing downstream may supply a domain fact the source did not state. An entry with gaps is therefore a classified entry with its gaps named, never a silent completion.

contract_version.description: The contract this instance declares. A consumer selects behaviour on this value and never infers a version from shape.

intake_id.description: Stable identifier for this intake, required for traceability. The caller supplies it: a producer that minted its own identifier could not have its run repeated and compared.

producer.description: The named producer. A const rather than a free string, so a result claiming another producer is not an instance of this contract.

source.description: What material was classified. It travels with the plan because an object derived from material that already existed records the source it was read from — the only record of whether a fact was stated by the business or read out of an artifact, now that a knowledge object carries no status to say so.

description.description: What the material is, in one sentence a reviewer can check against the artifacts named beside it.

artifacts.description: Each artifact the material was read from, by path or by stable reference. Non-empty: a classification whose source cannot be named cannot be reviewed, because nothing states what would have to be re-read to check it.

state.description: The closed outcome the consumer branches on. `classified` means every construct reached a decision, including the ones whose decision is that they have no home in the mapping. `blocked` means the classification could not be reached at all — the material is unintelligible, or a required input is absent.

blocking_reason.description: Why the classification could not be reached. Required on `blocked` and forbidden otherwise: a blocking reason on a successful result says two things at once.

entries.description: One entry per construct that reached a node type. Ordered by `proposed_id` so that two classifications of one input are comparable without a diff tool reordering them.

unmapped.description: Constructs the ontology's mapping has no home for. Recorded rather than forced into the nearest type: the mapping is closed, and a construct with no entry in it is not recorded until the mapping names its home.

notes.description: What a reviewer needs that no field above carries — an ambiguity the producer resolved one way and could have resolved another. Prose, and nothing branches on it.

construct.description: What the source material called it. Kept verbatim, so a reviewer can find it in the material rather than guessing which construct an identifier came from.

node_type.description: The node type this construct becomes. The vocabulary is the ontology's closed set of six; a plan naming a seventh is rejected at the boundary rather than authored and rejected later.

ddd.description: The DDD construct the entry records, as the value the object's `ddd` field will carry. Deliberately not constrained per node type here: knowledge-object.json holds that pairing conditionally and is the single authority for it, and a second copy would drift from the first.

boundary.description: The boundary identifier the authored object will declare. Absent only for a bounded-context boundary, which declares none — that absence is what identifies a partition root, and it is checked when the object is authored.

proposed_id.description: The identifier the object will take, computed from the node type and the boundary by the ontology's id arithmetic rather than allocated. No id allocator exists, and an id that cannot be computed from a path is one a consumer has to look up.

gaps.description: Every fact the node type requires that the source material does not supply. An empty array is a claim that the material is complete for this construct, and it is checkable: the authoring step blocks on a fact it was not given, so a wrongly empty array surfaces there rather than becoming an invention.

field.description: The frontmatter field or attribute parameter the material leaves unstated, named as the contract names it.

why.description: What the material would have to say for the field to be filled. A gap that says only 'missing' leaves the reader to work out what to ask for.

construct.description: What the source material called it, verbatim.

reason.description: Why no node type is right for it. The two ordinary answers are that it is stack knowledge the ontology excludes, and that it is rationale, which belongs in a decision record and never in a knowledge object.
